A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment. Their complete text, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning, reinforcement-learning, SAE steering and realignment experiments, with additional reward-hacking and human-data results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on model size and helpful-assistant features.

M1.justification: Appendix J extends feature discovery to the 1,000 latents with the largest activation decreases, selecting interventions for their ability to restore alignment through positive steering. This complements the original increased-activation search while retaining the SAE architecture and core steering procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds a limited conversational-role test, sampling answers to the same questions as an assistant versus a user. Dataset and domain coverage otherwise remains stable: the model-size experiments reuse existing health and automotive datasets.

E2.justification: The existing original-model, correct-data, safety-training and non-reward-hacking comparisons are retained. The additions examine model configurations and features within the proposed steering approach without introducing a distinct baseline method.

E3.justification: Section 2.4 introduces a systematic GPT-4o-family size/pretraining-compute sweep, using lightweight formatting SFT before correct or incorrect health/automotive training. Appendix J adds complementary steering and conversational-role controls. These extend the experimental design; the existing evaluation metrics and protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds model-size sensitivity analysis, including the small-model incoherence boundary, in Figures 4 and 34. Appendix J substantially extends the mechanistic investigation with decreased-activation features, bidirectional steering tests, assistant-token inspection and assistant-versus-user activation comparisons.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly reports standard deviation across dataset curves. This measures cross-dataset variation, not repeated-run uncertainty. Existing disclosures of three seeds for the main fine-tuning experiment and one seed for the sarcasm analysis are unchanged.

E6.justification: New results show increasing emergent misalignment with scale among sufficiently coherent models. Appendix J reports that latent #-1 restores all examined misaligned models to at most 1% misalignment and 1% incoherence, while many helpful features cannot induce misalignment when negatively steered. Previously reported results are retained.

T1.justification: The revisions add empirical procedures and interpretations, without new or revised formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and concluding discussion retain the claims about diverse emergent-misalignment settings, persona-feature control, and detection or mitigation. The new studies supplement these headline claims.

C2.justification: Appendix J expands the interpretation to suppression of helpful-assistant features and explicitly cautions that their apparent realignment advantage may reflect selection bias. Section 2.4 adds a competence-based interpretation of small-model scores and a data-efficiency hypothesis for the scaling trend.

D1.justification: v2 documents the formatting-SFT stage for the size experiments and the decreased-feature selection and assistant-token inspections in Appendix J. Existing SAE and fine-tuning hyperparameters, dataset instructions and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. The new analyses introduce no additional cited research.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 2.4 and Appendices F and J, updates cross-references, and adds two authors and their contribution statements. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 34 add aggregate and per-dataset scaling plots; Figure 41 adds helpful-feature steering and activation plots. Existing figures and tables are largely preserved but relocated and renumbered, with local layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The scaling analysis clarifies a coherence-related applicability boundary, while Appendix J addresses the previously unexplored decreasing-activation features and strengthens the mechanistic evidence. Its selection-bias caveat appropriately limits the realignment comparison. These are useful additions, although the new experiments have limited configuration and replication detail and leave the main argument largely unchanged.
